mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST < previous 12-month average) signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < 12-mo moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of persistent unemployment above 4.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decrease in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS below their 12-month averages signals a deflationary monetary easing, which increases real interest rates and discourages investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 12-mo average AND FEDFUNDS < 12-mo average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered deflationary easing episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5%) coincident with a stable unemployment rate signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in a non-recessionary regime.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% AND UNRATE stable (|UNRATE change| < 0.1%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of rapid payroll growth with stable unemployment in non-recessionary regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month average, combined with a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a slowdown in economic activity and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo average AND GDPC1 monthly change < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes of increased savings and declining consumption.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between monthly housing starts (HOUST) growth and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns, as new construction activity signals optimism and economic expansion, which boosts equity valuations in the short term.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly HOUST growth and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over a 5-year rolling window.
